text:
samira: FYI - enterprise customer reported widespread 401s right after we rotated their API keys. They claim some services still accept old tokens even after revocation. Repro steps and logs below, can someone pick this up?

laura_support: Can you paste the customer org + sample request/response (headers + minimal body)? Also which rotation path they used (vault rewrap / direct KMS)?

samira: Org: acme-inc, app: acme-ingest. They said we rotated via Vault "revoke-and-rotate" UI (uses KMS alias rewrap). Sample curl they ran:

```
curl -v -H "Authorization: Bearer eyJhbGciOi...OLDTOKEN..." \
  https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate -d '{"prompt":"hi"}'
```

Response (edge): 401 Unauthorized
Response (ingest LB log): 200 OK, upstream request accepted

Logs from edge (truncated):
```
EDGE: auth_check token_id=old-key-123 result=allowed source=cache ttl=42s
INGRESS: proxy_upstream trace_id=abc123 status=200 route=/v1/generate
AUTHZ-SERVICE: lookup token=old-key-123 status=revoked
```

samira: So edge cached the decision and returned 401 to client while upstream accepted? weird. customer sees 401s intermittently.

alex_engineer: Looks like two-level problem: (1) token revocation propagated to authz-service but (2) edge/ingress cache still had allow decision or stale connection. Ask for timeline: when did they rotate vs when errors started?

samira: Rotation started 2025-11-02T02:03Z, customer started seeing errors ~02:05Z.

jordan_ops: Possible keep-alive reuse to upstreams with old TLS session or old credential in sidecar. Which sidecars are in front of edge (envoy, nginx)? Also CDN?

samira: Envoy on edge + local ingress sidecar on the ingest cluster. CDN (fast-edge) in front with 30s cache TTL on auth decisions.

alex_engineer: That CDN TTL is suspicious. If auth decisions are cached by CDN and we don't purge, clients with in-flight sessions might hit cached deny/allow. Need to check auth-decision cache invalidation path when Vault revokes.

samira: I asked customer to upload full header capture. They included X-Request-ID=abc1234.

ops-bot: [incident-note] Noted: request abc1234 seen at edge 2025-11-02T02:05:12Z. Auth-check returned cached=false? (see detail)

samira: Pasted the authz debug from edge: `auth_cache.hit=true decision=allow cached_at=2025-11-02T02:04:45 expires_in=20s upstream_status=200`

alex_engineer: Steps I'd run: (A) confirm Vault shows token revoked: `vault kv get -format=json secret/apikeys/acme-inc` then `vault token-lookup OLDTOKEN` (B) check KMS alias rewrap logs (C) check CDN auth cache entries for that token id and purge.

samira: Ran `vault token-lookup OLDTOKEN` - response: token not found / revoked. KMS rewrap confirmed success at 02:03:55Z.

jordan_ops: Ok so backend state is correct. Next: purge edge auth caches and restart ingress sidecar for the complaining pods. Commands I used:

```
kubectl -n acme-ingest exec deploy/ingress-sidecar -- curl -s http://127.0.0.1:9900/cache/purge?key=old-key-123
kubectl -n acme-ingest rollout restart deploy/ingest-sidecar
```

jordan_ops: Also purged CDN: `fastedge invalidate --path /auth/decisions?token_id=old-key-123`

samira: After we purged caches and restarted sidecars, the customer reported errors dropped to zero within 45s. They confirmed calls started succeeding with new token. :thumbsup:

laura_support: Great. Two follow-ups: (1) Need postmortem note for why CDN TTL didn't get updated on rotation; (2) We should add a forced cache-invalidate webhook to rotation flow.

alex_engineer: Agreed. Engineering action items: 1) Add rotation hook that triggers CDN invalidate + edge cache purge; 2) Add telemetry that ties token_id to CDN cache entries so we can purge by token id; 3) Short-term: lower CDN auth-decision TTL from 30s to 5s for rotations-in-progress flag.

samira: I'll file a support follow-up to the customer and add step-by-step workaround in KB: "If 401s after rotation, purge edge caches + restart sidecar."

vault-bot: Vault audit: revocation event for secret=secret/apikeys/acme-inc token_id=old-key-123 time=2025-11-02T02:03:50Z

ops-bot: Note: we observed a ~20s gap between revoke and CDN invalidation due to missing hook. Tickets: ENG-9998 (rotation -> cache purge hook), INFRA-445 (CDN TTL policy).

alex_engineer: I'll pick ENG-9998. Quick patch: rotation job should POST to `/hooks/purge-cache` with { "token_id": "old-key-123" }.

samira: Customer confirmed resolution and will keep an eye; they requested SLA credit for the 2 minutes of degraded traffic, forwarded to billing.

laura_support: Thanks team. Closing thread after ENG/INFRA tickets created and KB updated. :white_check_mark:
